gloss: the underworld; the realm of the dead; Hades

definitions.gloss: the underworld; the realm of the dead; the afterlife
definitions.explanation: The world of the dead in Buddhist and Japanese folk belief. The place where souls go after death.

examples.japanese: {冥土|めいど}の{旅|たび}に{出|で}る。
examples.english: To depart on the journey to the underworld.

examples.japanese: {冥土|めいど}の{土産|みやげ}にいい{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いた。
examples.english: I heard a good story — something to take with me to the grave.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は「{冥土|めいど}で{祖父|そふ}に{会|あ}えるのが{楽|たの}しみだ」と{冗談|じょうだん}を{言|い}っていた。
examples.english: My grandmother joked that she looked forward to meeting grandfather in the afterlife.

notes:
A Buddhist-derived concept referring to the dark underworld where the dead reside. Also written as {冥途|めいど}. The word appears frequently in set expressions and idioms.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {冥土|めいど}の{土産|みやげ}: a story or experience to "take to the grave" — something memorable heard or experienced late in life
- {冥土|めいど}の{旅|たび}: the journey to the afterlife — dying
- {冥土|めいど}に{旅立|たびだ}つ: to depart for the afterlife — a euphemism for dying

SIMILAR WORDS:
- あの{世|よ}: the other world; the afterlife — the most common everyday term
- {黄泉|よみ}: the land of the dead — from Shinto mythology; archaic and literary
- {地獄|じごく}: hell — a place of punishment, unlike {冥土|めいど} which is neutral
- {浄土|じょうど}: Pure Land — the Buddhist paradise, a positive afterlife destination

USAGE:
Not to be confused with the homophone メイド (maid), which is a loanword from English.
